_readme: MUTATION CATALOG — the structural guard for 'tests that pass for the wrong reason' (issue #112).
Each entry names ONE security-critical mechanism, an exact anchor string in the source that
IS that mechanism, a mutation that removes it, and the test files that CLAIM to cover it.
`node scripts/mutation-guard.mjs` applies each mutation in turn, runs only the claimed tests,
and reports SURVIVED for any mutant those tests still pass against. A survivor is not a bug in
the source — it is a hole in the tests, which is the thing #112 found six of.
`packages/core/test/mutation-catalog.test.ts` runs in the ordinary `pnpm test` and asserts that
every `anchor` still occurs EXACTLY ONCE in its `file`, and that every `tests` path exists. That
is what keeps this catalog from rotting into a no-op: a refactor that moves a mechanism breaks
the catalog loudly instead of silently turning its mutant into a no-op edit.
MOSTLY security-critical mechanisms, and one (#152) that is not: whether capwall's ESM install
starts Node's module-customization THREAD is a startup-cost invariant. It earns a mutant on the
same argument the security ones do — going back to `module.register()` breaks nothing and fails
nothing, and silently puts ~53 ms of thread bootstrap back on every mediated process (and, on
Node 26, a DEP0205 warning on stderr). A property no test asserts is a property that decays,
`needsBuild` marks mutants whose claimed tests spawn a subprocess against `dist/` — those need
a rebuild after mutating and after restoring.

mutants.mechanism: #21 — collapse runs of `**` segments so a glob compiles to ONE unbounded group (ReDoS hardening)

mutants.mechanism: #97 — a hardened install pins the capwall-installed global egress functions writable:false, even when an un-hardened install built them
mutants.anchor: slot.pin(replacement); // best-effort — a global someone made non-configurable is reported below

mutants.mechanism: #98 — the env-gate suspension during a real spawn is scoped to the exact keys Node itself reads, not a blanket 'gate off' window
#60/#86 — the dgram auto-bind replay token is single-use, so a dependency that reads `socket.send` cannot keep an un-gated send around
#133/#143 — when the shortened capture reaches nothing it may believe, attribution re-runs the VERBATIM full walk; 'found nothing' is never an answer, and never the `<app>` trust root
mutants.note: The fail-open the boundary fast path could reintroduce: three nested evals fill the whole prefix with OPAQUE frames, and a decline that answers `<app>` hands the trust root to any dependency willing to call eval.

mutants.mechanism: #133/#143 — the fast path stands down entirely below the frame budget at which 'the short capture found it' still implies 'the full capture would have found it too', rather than offering a second opinion the full walk could not reach
#143 — capwall's OWN frames are never a principal. V8 skips them on the fast path and the walk skips them on the fallback; the two must agree, or a declined capture attributes the shim itself
mutants.anchor: if (source.startsWith(CAPWALL_ROOT + path.sep)) continue; // capwall's own machinery
mutants.mutation: if (false && source.startsWith(CAPWALL_ROOT + path.sep)) continue; // capwall's own machinery
mutants.note: Only observable on the FALLBACK path, which is exactly why it needs a mutant: the fast path skips those frames in V8 and would hide the loss.

mutants.mechanism: #152/#153 — capwall's ESM interception uses the SYNCHRONOUS module.registerHooks(), so no module-customization thread is started (~53 ms) and no DEP0205 deprecation warning is printed. module.register() is Stability 0 with removal announced
mutants.anchor: hooks = pristineRegisterHooks.call(realModule, { resolve, load }) as RegisteredHooks;
mutants.mutation:
hooks = pristineRegisterHooks.call(realModule, { resolve, load }) as RegisteredHooks;
    realModule.register("data:text/javascript,export function resolve(s,c,n){return n(s,c)}", import.meta.url);
mutants.note: The one mutant in this catalog that ADDS rather than removes, because the invariant is an absence. It re-creates exactly the cost #152 removed — the loader thread — without changing a single behaviour, which is why nothing but a dedicated probe catches it.

mutants.mechanism: #62/#152 — the LAST uninstall() deregisters the module hooks, so ESM teardown is real rather than best-effort and a never-imported specifier is un-mediated afterwards exactly as it is on the CJS path, instead of throwing a bridge error that permanently poisons the specifier
mutants.note: module.register() could not offer this line at all — the asymmetry docs/threat-model.md used to carry as a known limit. Without it the hooks outlive their install and #62's swap fixture reports the pre-#152 behaviour.

mutants.mechanism: #78/#61 — the load hook re-mediates any raw node:<mediated> URL it is handed, since capwall's own resolve never emits one. Since #152 this is reachable only from a SYNCHRONOUS hook registered after capwall's, which is the one attacker position still ahead of capwall in the chain
mutants.note: Had no mutant while the register() chain also reached it and two tests covered it. It now has exactly one route and one test, so it needs one.

mutants.mechanism: #170 — the real Request.prototype.url getter is captured at MODULE EVALUATION, before any dependency can replace it; only a process that has already switched the guard off (CAPWALL_GLOBAL_EGRESS=0) defers it
mutants.note: Deferring the capture to install() for EVERYONE is the obvious way to buy back the ~21 ms and it reopens #26/#56 on the embedder path: a dependency required between `import @capwall/core` and `install()` replaces the prototype getter, undici keeps dialing the real URL, and capwall guards the attacker's chosen one.

mutants.mechanism: #170 — a getter-only member of the real `http` namespace is mirrored onto the shim as a getter, so building the shim does not read `WebSocket`/`CloseEvent`/`MessageEvent` and does not materialize undici
mutants.anchor: return desc !== undefined && desc.get !== undefined && desc.set === undefined;
mutants.note: A startup-cost invariant rather than a security property, on the same argument as `esm-no-loader-thread`: flattening the copy breaks nothing and fails nothing, and silently puts ~21 ms of undici materialization back on every mediated process that requires `http` — including every ESM one, which builds the registry eagerly.

mutants.mechanism: #156 — the Web Storage guard patches NOTHING unless this process actually has Web Storage, and it answers that question with Object.keys(globalThis) rather than by reading the global (which prints an ExperimentalWarning on Node 26)
mutants.note: Runs on every supported Node — it is the ABSENT case, which is the half a version-gated feature usually leaves unasserted. A guard that installs unconditionally registers a process-patch site on 22 and 24 where there is nothing to patch.

mutants.mechanism: #156 — localStorage's six members take an fs decision on the resolved --localstorage-file path (read for getItem/key/length, write for setItem/removeItem/clear) before Node performs the file I/O below the fs shim
mutants.note: The mechanism only exists on Node >=26 with --localstorage-file, so its claimed tests skipIf away below that and the mutant would report SURVIVED for a reason that is not about the tests. Reported SKIPPED by name instead. Verified CAUGHT on a real 26.5.0 binary.

mutants.mechanism: #123/#177 — the module-read gate sits on `Module.prototype.load`, the point Node commits to a filename, and is handed Node's OWN resolution result. Every CJS route reaches it: require, require.resolve-then-require, a direct Module._load with any isMain/parent/options bag, require(esm), the entry point, and `new Module(f).load(f)` — which never touches Module._load at all, so the pre-#177 gate could not see it even in principle
mutants.note: The mutation leaves the call site and the import in place and makes the gate unreachable — so a test that only asserts 'capwall is installed', or that the patch site is registered, still passes. It is the whole of #123 at its new home: with it applied, a deny-all enforce policy lets any dependency require any file on disk with zero decisions.

mutants.mechanism: #177 — the gate consults NOTHING the caller can set. `Module._load(secret, undefined, true)` makes Node stamp `module.id = '.'` and `process.mainModule = module` for the forged load, exactly as it does for the real entry point, so neither is evidence of anything. The process root is identified from HOST facts instead (process.argv[1], and the resolve hook's parentless non-`require` resolution) — see loader/module-read.ts § hostRootTargets
mutants.mutation: if (typeof filename === "string" && (this as { id?: unknown }).id !== ".") guardCjsModuleRead(ctx, filename);
mutants.note: This is #177 rewritten against the new architecture, and it is the mutation a reviewer would actually propose: `id === '.'` LOOKS like Node's own statement that this is the entry point. It is Node's own statement — about an argument the caller passed. Sharing an anchor with `module-read-gate-at-proto-load` is deliberate: that one asks whether the gate is there, this one asks whether it can be talked out of firing.

mutants.mechanism: #177/#180 — the resolve hook decides `import` and nothing else. Since #152 it is consulted for `require()` too, and on THAT path `context.parentURL` is derived from the `parent` module record handed to Module._load, i.e. from an ordinary argument. Declining every `require`-conditioned resolution is what leaves those loads to guardCjsModuleRead, whose subject is a stack walk
mutants.note: Replaces `esm-gate-stands-down-only-for-require`, whose mechanism (a depth counter over a whole Module._load) was #179. The mutation is fail-open in TWO ways at once: the hook charges whichever principal the caller named (#180), and a `require`-conditioned resolution with no `parent` reaches the parentless branch and RECORDS the attacker's target as a process root, which then exempts it from the CJS gate as well (#177). It is also merely noisy in a third (two decisions per require), which is what `records ONE decision for one require` pins.

mutants.mechanism: #177 — the process-root record is written ONLY by a resolution Node performed for itself: no importer, and not the `require` condition. That is the one signal on this path no in-process caller can produce, and it is what replaced believing `isMain`. A record written for a load that HAS an importer would let any dependency nominate a file as the process root and then load it freely
mutants.note: The mutation is the plausible over-reach — 'record every resolved target, the CJS half will only match the real entry anyway' — and it converts the entry-point exemption from a host fact back into something a dependency writes: one denied `import(secret)` makes the subsequent `require(secret)` free. Caught by the unit rows that assert a load WITH an importer records nothing.

mutants.mechanism: #61/#181 — the loader-hook gate is a patch on `Module.register`/`Module.registerHooks` THEMSELVES, so every route to the capability converges on it: the named ESM export, `require('node:module').registerHooks`, `Module.registerHooks` reached through node:module's own self-reference, `module.constructor.registerHooks` (which needs no require at all) and `process.getBuiltinModule('node:module')`
mutants.note: The mutation leaves the patch installed, the site registered and the shim intact — so `process-patch-sites.test.ts`'s inventory and the shim's own structural test both still pass. It is the whole of #61 at its new home: with it applied, any dependency registers a resolve+load hook that de-mediates node:fs process-wide, and an innocent third package reads a secret with no capwall line at all.

mutants.mechanism: #181 — the node:module shim's `get` trap never hands back the raw module object. Node keeps a legacy self-reference (`Module.Module === Module`), so a trap that forwards every value verbatim hands a caller an un-shimmed route to the surface it is shimming, through the shim
mutants.note: Deliberately claimed by a STRUCTURAL test, not a behavioural one. Since #181 moved the capability gate onto the two function objects, the raw class no longer behaves differently from the proxy — so no end-to-end fixture can catch this, and the property is worth keeping anyway: it is what stops the shim being the thing that undoes the NEXT member gate, which is exactly how #181 happened.

mutants.mechanism: #183 — capwall's synthetic `capwall-esm:` URL is an `import`-path answer only. A `require` resolution's answer is a value the caller can see (`require.resolve`) and must be able to feed back into `require`, so it gets Node's own URL — otherwise `Module.isBuiltin` answers false for all 24 mediated spellings and `require(require.resolve('fs'))` throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND
mutants.anchor: if (!isCjsResolution(context.conditions)) return { url: PREFIX + specifier, shortCircuit: true };
mutants.mutation: if (true) return { url: PREFIX + specifier, shortCircuit: true };
mutants.note: Claimed by the IN-PROCESS rows that call the hook directly, not by the subprocess differential — Node only routes `require.resolve` through the hook chain on >=24.18, so a subprocess-only claim would make this mutant survive on the floor and need a `minNodeMajor` that major-granularity cannot express (24.5.0 behaves like 22 here). Calling the hook removes the version from the question entirely.
